See All Entertainment

As head of Splice, Kakul has tried to carefully thread the line on AI music tools. She also hates her cup warmer.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Kakul Srivastava is the CEO of Splice, the sample platform countless producers rely on for one-shots and melodic loops. Samples pulled from the service have found their way into massive hits like Lisa’s “Money” and “Espresso” by Sabrina Carpenter. (The original samples are here and here, for the curious.)

Before that, Kakul held executive roles at Flickr, Yahoo, GitHub, and Adobe. Throughout her career, Kakul has found herself at the intersection of Silicon Valley and creatives. That’s been especially true at Splice, where she’s not just expanded the platform’s footprint by acquiring Spitfire Audio, but also overseen its forays into the world of generative AI.

Last year, she was very outspoken on an episode of Decoder about avoiding the sort of “push-button, get-song” AI that has made companies like Suno so controversial. And based on her answers to our questionnaire, it doesn’t seem like her skepticism has waned. When it comes to Splice, the company has made a point of trying to offer AI products that still keep the human at the center of the creative process. And when it comes to communicating with colleagues, Kakul sees the same need to keep AI at bay.

What is your most indispensable tool?

A well-written document and a real conversation about it.

Splice is remote-first, so we don’t have a hallway. What we have instead is somebody sitting down and actually thinking something through, and then a bunch of people arguing with it. Almost everything good that’s happened here started that way.

Which is why I’m careful about AI-written documents. Once you can’t tell whether there’s a person behind the words, the conversation you have about it becomes a different conversation, and a worse one. And you can’t really go back from that. I think the same thing is true of music.

What is your happy place online?

Instagram, which I know is not the fashionable answer. My feed has turned into almost entirely people making music in ways I would never have thought of. There’s gothic western, which I did not know was a thing. There’s a woman in Russia who organizes street dancing. There’s a guy playing modern hits on a hammered dulcimer. The Indian chai-wala rapping. I could watch it all, all day.

What game do you have the fondest memories of?

Antakshari. It’s an Indian game — you sing a bit of a song, and whatever letter the line ends on is the letter the next person has to start their song with. You play it on long car rides, at weddings, any time a group of people is stuck somewhere together.

I love that the whole game is made out of music and none of the players are musicians. You just have to remember, and you have to be willing to sing in front of your family, which for most people is the harder part. And then when you watch people’s faces get soft when the song really hits — even when it’s sung badly. That’s the power of music.

What’s the most disappointing gadget you’ve owned?

A cup warmer. It warms the cup. It does not warm the coffee. I want to be clear that it works exactly as designed.

What creation are you most proud of?

I can’t not say my kids. Watching a person go from nothing to a fully formed human with opinions you did not give them is the most amazing thing I have been anywhere near. And the strange part is that it isn’t rare. It’s happening in every house on the street. We all just watch it happen and then go about our day.

Which are you least proud of?

I was on the early team at Tiny Speck, the company that later became Slack. Before Slack, we made a game called Glitch — a massively multiplayer open world — and it was one of the most beautiful things I’ve ever worked on. The art, the sound, the writing, the way the world actually worked. Some of the most talented people I’ve ever been around.

It failed, and it failed for reasons that were sitting right there in front of us. It was built on Flash, and Adobe had already stopped investing in Flash. It was a PC experience at the exact moment the whole world was moving to playing games on a phone. Two enormous tectonic trends, and we didn’t account for either one in time to do anything about them. I feel like I let down the creativity of the people who built something beautiful.

What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?

Say the thing, then explain it. Don’t lay all your proof out first, hoping it earns you the right to make your point. Nobody is listening to the proof yet. They’re listening for whether you sound like you believe it. The confidence you say it with is what makes room for the explanation.

What is your current obsession?

Cooking my mother’s food. She died before I learned most of it from her, so I’ve been reconstructing her recipes off YouTube — strangers in their own kitchens, making the thing the way their mothers made it. It takes a lot of tries. I got one of them right last year, and the taste put me straight back to being eight years old with my mom by my side.

This is what I think about when people ask me what technology is for. Some guy uploaded a video of his family’s recipe and gave me my mother’s cooking back. He will never know that.

What do you think is worth splurging on?

Live jazz. There is nothing else like being in a room where people are making decisions in real time and can’t take them back. I travel a lot for work, and if there’s any way to get to a show in whatever city I’m in, I’ll do it, even when it means I’m useless the next morning.

What would the tagline for your biopic be?

A heist movie where nothing gets stolen and everybody gets paid.

What’s the last GIF or meme you used?

如果您通过文内链接购买商品，The Verge可能会获得佣金。请参阅我们的职业道德声明。

卡库尔·斯里瓦斯塔瓦（Kakul Srivastava）是Splice的首席执行官。无数制作人都依赖这个音频采样平台获取单发采样（one-shots）与旋律循环片段（melodic loops）。该平台上的音频采样曾被用于众多大热单曲，例如Lisa的《Money》和萨布丽娜·卡彭特（Sabrina Carpenter）的《Espresso》。（感兴趣的读者可以在这里和这里找到原始采样片段。）

在此之前，卡库尔曾先后在Flickr、雅虎、GitHub和Adobe担任高管职务。在她的整个职业生涯中，卡库尔始终身处硅谷与创意人士的交汇点。在Splice尤其如此——她不仅通过收购Spitfire Audio扩大了平台的版图，还亲自操刀引领其迈向生成式AI领域。

去年，她在播客节目《Decoder》中直言不讳地表示，要避免走向“按个按钮就出首歌”的那种AI模式——正是这种模式让Suno等公司备受争议。从她对我们调查问卷的回答来看，她的这种审慎与怀疑态度丝毫未减。在Splice，公司一直坚持提供仍以人类为创意核心的AI产品。而在与同事沟通时，卡库尔同样认为有必要与AI保持距离。

你最不可或缺的工具是什么？
一份撰写精良的文档，以及围绕它展开的真实对话。
Splice推行远程优先办公，所以我们没有茶水间或走廊可以闲聊。取而代之的是，某个人坐下来认真把一件事想透，然后一群人围绕它进行辩论与争论。我们这里几乎所有美好的成果，都是以这种方式诞生的。
这也是为什么我对AI撰写的文档保持警惕。一旦你无法确定文字背后是否有真人在思考，围绕它展开的对话就会变味，变得更糟糕。而那一步一旦跨出，你就很难再回头了。我认为音乐也是同一个道理。

你在网络上的快乐源泉是什么？
Instagram，我知道这算不上什么时髦的答案。我的信息流现在几乎全是人们用我想都想不到的方式做音乐的内容。有我以前闻所未闻的“哥特西部风”（gothic western）；有一位在俄罗斯组织街舞的女士；有一个人用扬琴演奏现代流行金曲；还有印度街头卖奶茶的小哥在说唱。我能津津有味地看上一整天。

你记忆最深的游戏是什么？
安塔克夏里（Antakshari）。这是一个印度传统游戏——你唱出一小段歌，最后一个歌词的发音字母，就是下一位玩家接唱歌曲的开头字母。在漫长的车程中、婚礼上，或者任何一群人被困在一起无事可做的时候，大家都会玩这个。
我喜欢这个游戏完全由音乐构成，而参与者却无一人是专业音乐人。你只需要去回忆，并且愿意当着家人的面放声歌唱——对大多数人来说，后一点才是更难的部分。然后，当你看到某首歌真正打动人心时，人们的表情变得温柔柔和——哪怕那首歌唱得跑调走音。这就是音乐的力量。

你买过最令人失望的科技数码小配件是什么？
一个暖杯垫。它把杯子热得滚烫，却根本热不到咖啡。不过我想说明的是，它的实际表现确实和设计完全一致。

你最引以为傲的创造是什么？
我不能不提我的孩子们。看着一个人从无到有，长成一个拥有自己独立见解的健全的人，而那些想法甚至不是你灌输给他们的，这是我所经历过的最神奇的事情。奇妙的是，这并不罕见。整条街上的每家每户都在发生着同样的事。我们都只是目睹着这一切发生，然后继续过着各自的日常生活。

你最不引以为傲的事情是什么？
我曾是Tiny Speck的早期团队成员，这家公司后来演变成了Slack。在做Slack之前，我们开发了一款名为《Glitch》的游戏——一个大型多人开放世界游戏，那是我参与过的最美妙的作品之一。无论是美术、声效、文案，还是这个虚拟世界的运作机制，全都出自一群我所接触过的最具才华的人之手。
但它失败了，而且失败的原因就摆在眼前。它是基于Flash开发的，而当时Adobe已经停止对Flash的投入；它是一款PC端游戏体验，而彼时整个世界正在全面转向手机游戏。两大翻天覆地的时代趋势，我们却都没有及时考虑到并采取应对措施。我觉得自己辜负了那些创造出如此美好事物的人的才华与创造力。

你听过最好的一条建议是什么？
先抛出核心观点，再去作解释。不要先摆出一堆论据，指望通过它们来赢得陈述观点的权利。那时候根本没人会在意你的论据；大家在听的是，你的语气是否听起来坚信不疑。你表达时的笃定与自信，才会为接下来的阐释留出空间。

你目前最着迷的事情是什么？
做我母亲做过的菜。在她把大部分手艺传给我之前就离世了，所以我一直在通过YouTube复刻她的食谱——看世界各地素不相识的人在自家的厨房里，按照各自母亲的做法烹饪。这需要反复尝试。去年我终于做对了一道，那个味道瞬间让我回到了八岁时依偎在母亲身边的时光。
当别人问我科技的意义何在时，我心里想到的就是这件事。某个陌生人上传了自己家族食谱的视频，却帮我找回了母亲的味道。而他可能永远都不会知道这一点。

你认为什么事情值得挥金如土？
现场爵士乐。那种大家在同一个空间里实时做决定且毫无退路的现场感，是无可替代的。我经常因公出差，无论身在哪座城市，只要有机会能赶去现场听一场演出，我都一定会去，哪怕这意味着第二天早上整个人彻底处于废人状态。

如果给你拍一部传记电影，宣传标语会是什么？
“一部什么都没被偷走，却人人都拿到了报酬的劫盗大片。”

financeStories.title: Vessev造出了一艘几乎是在“飞行”的电动水翼渡轮
financeStories.originalTitle: Vessev built an electric ferry that almost flies
financeStories.snippet: Vessev hopes its electric hydrofoil ferry will change the way people and cities think about boats.
financeStories.fullContent:
“When will we start flying?” I asked Vessev co-founder and CEO Eric Laakmann, as we pulled away from the Brooklyn marina in the startup’s VS-9 electric ferry. “We already are.”

I’ll admit I was a bit disappointed. I thought the moment when it transitioned from sailing like a regular boat to almost-flying as a surface-skimming hydrofoil would be more … momentous.

I’ve been on my share of boats, including large ferries, small sailboats, and plenty of others in between, but never been on a hydrofoil and I was curious what flying along the water might feel like during the brief ride from the Brooklyn Marina out toward Governors Island on the East River in New York.

It didn’t feel like flying, but it was a bit like a riding in a sports car.

Traditional boats of this size — about 30 feet — start to bounce and slap the water as they gain speed. But on a hydrofoil, that’s when the foils start to do their work.

On the surface, the VS-9 looks like plenty of other catamarans. But under the hull are two wing-like structures that lift the boat as they slice through the water. Computer-controlled underwater flaps keep the ride smooth and stable. In the VS-9, most of the lifting is done by the front foil, with about 20% handled by the rear.

The rear foil also hosts the electric motor, which Vessev makes in-house. Why not outsource it? Laakmann said that it’s important to keep costs in line — eventually, you’ll have to bring production in house, so why not do it earlier in development? The only thing Vessev doesn’t build are the batteries. “Those have been commoditized,” Laakmann said.

By lifting the hull clear of the water, hydrofoils can operate more efficiently than other boats. That’s especially important for electric boats, where every kilowatt-hour counts.

Shipbuilders have been experimenting with hydrofoils for well over a century. The design offers several advantages, including lower drag and a smoother ride. The subtle transition I experienced on the VS-9, from sailing to almost-flying, underlined just how smooth a hydrofoil can be.

Despite hydrofoils’ advantages, they’re not a panacea. The design works best in waters the boat can clear when sailing on its foils. For the VS-9, that’s about two and a half feet, or 0.75 meters. If the waves go higher than that, they start hitting the hull, ruining the smooth ride and sapping some efficiency. While they’re not ideal for the open ocean, hydrofoils make sense for other waterways, including lakes, rivers, and bays.

Vessev, which raised a $19 million Series A in August, is targeting transit operations to start. Laakmann thinks the combination of electric propulsion and hydrofoils can bring down the cost of operating smaller vessels and make them comfortable enough that they could augment urban mass transit systems.

Somewhere like New York City could use them to zip people to Brooklyn or Queens without needing to build much new infrastructure.

Hotels and tour operators are also an early target market, and public demonstrations like the one I attended have attracted wealthy individuals looking for another toy, Laakmann said.

For now, the VS-9 I rode is one of a kind, but Laakmann said Vessev plans to build more. Eventually, the company might shift to producing electric hydrofoil kits, allowing other boatbuilders to design their own vessels around the technology, Laakmann said.

Senior Reporter, Climate

Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor.

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.

“我们什么时候开始起飞？”当这艘初创公司的VS-9电动渡轮驶离布鲁克林码头时，我向Vessev联合创始人兼首席执行官埃里克·拉克曼（Eric Laakmann）问道。“我们已经在飞了。”

我承认当时我有点失望。我还以为从像普通船只那样航行过渡到像贴水掠过的水翼艇那样“几乎在飞行”的时刻，会显得更加……惊心动魄。

我坐过不少船，包括大型渡轮、小型帆船以及介于两者之间的各种船只，但从未坐过水翼艇；在从布鲁克林码头出发、沿纽约东河驶向总督岛的短暂行程中，我很好奇贴水飞行的感觉会是怎样的。

它感觉并不像在飞，但有点像坐在一辆跑车里。

这种尺寸（约30英尺）的传统船只在加速时会开始颠簸并拍打水面。但在水翼船上，那正是水翼开始大显身手的时刻。

表面上看，VS-9与许多其他双体船颇为相似。但在船体下方有两个翼状结构，在切开水面时将船体托起。由计算机控制的水下襟翼使航行保持平稳。在VS-9上，大部分升力由前水翼提供，后水翼承担约20%。

后水翼还搭载了由Vessev自主制造的电动机。为什么不外包？拉克曼表示，控制成本非常重要——最终你总得转为自研自产，那么为什么不在研发早期就这么做呢？Vessev唯一不自行制造的是电池。“那些已经是高度商品化的通用产品了，”拉克曼说。

通过将船体完全抬离水面，水翼船的运行效率比其他船只更高。这对于每一度电（千瓦时）都至关重要的电动船只尤为关键。

造船工人对水翼的探索已有了一个多世纪。这种设计具有多项优势，包括阻力更小、行驶更平稳。我在VS-9上体验到的那种从航行到“几乎在飞”的细微过渡，恰恰凸显了水翼船究竟有多平稳。

尽管水翼具有种种优势，但它们并非万灵药。这种设计在水波高度不影响船只依靠水翼抬起航行的水域中表现最佳。对VS-9而言，这个高度约为2.5英尺（约0.75米）。如果浪高超过这一标准，波浪就会开始冲击船体，破坏平稳的乘坐感并降低部分效率。虽然它们并不适合公海大洋，但水翼船对于湖泊、河流和海湾等其他水路非常契合。

今年8月刚完成1900万美元A轮融资的Vessev，首先将目标瞄准了公共交通运营。拉克曼认为，电力推进与水翼的结合能够降低小型船只的运营成本，并提供足够的舒适度，从而可以补充城市大众交通运输系统。

像纽约市这样的地方可以利用它们快速将乘客送往布鲁克林或皇后区，而无需新建太多基础设施。

拉克曼表示，酒店和旅游运营商也是早期的目标市场，像我参加的这种公开演示活动还吸引了寻找新玩具的富裕人士。

目前，我乘坐的VS-9还是独一无二的原型船，但拉克曼表示Vessev计划建造更多。他提到，最终该公司可能会转向生产电动水翼套件，允许其他造船厂围绕这项技术设计自己的船只。

蒂姆·德尚（Tim De Chant）是TechCrunch的资深气候记者。他曾为多家出版物撰稿，包括《连线》杂志、《芝加哥论坛报》、Ars Technica、《连线中国》（The Wire China）以及他担任创刊编辑的NOVA Next。
德尚还是麻省理工学院（MIT）科学写作研究生项目的讲师，并于2018年获得麻省理工学院奈特科学新闻奖学金（Knight Science Journalism Fellowship），期间研究了气候技术并探索了新闻业的新商业模式。他拥有加州大学伯克利分校环境科学、政策与管理学博士学位，以及圣奥拉夫学院环境研究、英语和生物学学士学位。

financeStories.fullContent:

David Robinson used to write safety reports at OpenAI and now says its culture is ‘broken’

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

David Robinson used to write the safety reports that accompanied every major model release at OpenAI. This week, he resigned from his position and is now speaking out in an editorial in The Atlantic.

It’s understandable if you’re feeling a bit cynical about everyone suddenly coming out of the woodwork to warn about how dangerous the thing they helped build is. They did, after all, make this mess. But that doesn’t mean we should discount their warnings.

Robinson says that the culture in industry is fundamentally broken. That this is a deeper issue than simply slapping a few new rules or regulations on how we handle training models. Silicon Valley has operated with “extreme confidence” and “perpetual sprints,” he says, building bigger and better models with “unimpeded optimism” that ignores or underestimates potential problems.

He says the time has come for AI companies to develop a sense of humility and look outside the insular, move-fast-and-break-things world of the tech industry. Specifically, he says AI needs nuclear-level safeguards:

Given today’s risks, frontier labs need to run like nuclear power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster.

Robinson is just the latest in a growing parade of researchers and safety workers who have left their positions at prominent AI firms. Jacob Coxon seems to have kicked off the exodus by quitting Anthropic and then publicly saying AI “could kill us all by the end of the decade.” He was followed by Robert O’Callahan, Bilal Chughtai, and Josh Engels at Google DeepMind, as well as Joe Benton at Anthropic.

戴维·罗宾逊曾负责撰写 OpenAI 每次重大模型发布时附带的安全报告。本周，他从该职位辞职，目前在《大西洋月刊》（The Atlantic）发表社论发声。

如果你对那些突然冒出来警告自己亲手打造的产物有多危险的人感到有些讽刺，这是可以理解的。毕竟，这个烂摊子确实是他们造成的。但这并不意味着我们应该对他们的警告置之不理。

罗宾逊表示，该行业的文化从根本上就已经崩坏了。这是一个更深层次的问题，绝非仅仅在如何处理模型训练上生硬地加上几条新规则或监管条例就能解决。他指出，硅谷一直带着“极度的自信”并在“永不停歇的冲刺”中运转，以“毫无阻碍的盲目乐观”打造更大、更好的模型，却忽视或低估了潜在的问题。

他表示，人工智能公司学会保持谦逊，并将目光投向科技行业这种固步自封、“快速行动、打破常规”的世界之外的时机已经到来。具体而言，他表示人工智能需要核电级别的安全保障：

“鉴于当今的风险，前沿实验室需要像核电站或繁忙的机场那样运转，配备多层冗余机制并进行周密、耗时的规划，以确保偶尔且不可避免的人为失误不会成为打开灾难之门的推手。”

罗宾逊只是离开知名人工智能公司的研究人员与安全从业人员队伍中最新的一员。雅各布·考克森（Jacob Coxon）似乎拉开了这场离职潮的序幕，他从 Anthropic 辞职，随后公开表示人工智能“可能会在十年内彻底消灭我们所有人”。紧随其后的有 Google DeepMind 的罗伯特·奥卡拉汉（Robert O’Callahan）、比拉尔·丘格泰（Bilal Chughtai）和乔希·恩格斯（Josh Engels），以及 Anthropic 的乔·本顿（Joe Benton）。

aiStories.title: 联邦法官称Flock属于“无差别的群体大规模监控”
aiStories.originalTitle: Federal judge calls Flock ‘indiscriminate mass surveillance’
aiStories.snippet: A federal judge ruled that a sheriff’s deputy violated a woman’s Fourth Amendment rights when using Flock to search for her license plate without a warrant.
aiStories.fullContent:
A federal judge ruled this week that a Tulsa, Oklahoma sheriff’s deputy violated a woman’s Fourth Amendment rights when using Flock Safety to search for her license plate without a warrant.

As reported by 404 Media, this ruling does not create a binding precedent, but it is one of the first times that a federal judge has ruled that a Flock search is unconstitutional.

In this case, Judge Sara Hill said the deputy should have obtained a warrant before searching the Flock database for the woman’s license plate, as he had “no apparent reason” for the search “other than the fact that [the woman’s vehicle] had a California license plate.”

The deputy then used the woman’s travel history in Flock as part of the justification for searching her car, where he allegedly discovered 91 pounds of meth. But Judge Hill wrote that all evidence obtained after the Flock search “must be suppressed as the fruit of a poisonous tree.”

Judge Hill also took broader aim at warrantless searches of the Flock database, writing that tracking people’s location — even when they’re in public places — becomes “constitutionally problematic when law enforcement can indiscriminately and passively catalog your whereabouts over an extended period of time and then use that information for any purpose whenever convenient.”

“This is a type of indiscriminate mass surveillance,” Hill wrote. “It is not targeted on a single individual, as in [Carpenter v. United States, a Supreme Court case focused on how government agencies access location data from cell phones]. It is a tool that collects information about all vehicles that pass by any network-connected camera at all times, and it serves up the information to law enforcement on demand.”

Hill joins a growing chorus of Flock critics from across the political spectrum. Numerous local and state governments, including Florida and Texas, have said they will stop using the technology. And on Friday, Senator Bernie Sanders — a Democrat from Vermont — introduced the Block Flock Act, which would bar federal agencies from using automated license plate readers such as Flock.

Flock CEO Garretty Langley — who we’ll be interviewing on-stage at TechCrunch Disrupt — has called for a “compromise” between privacy and safety and offered an apology to women who have been stalked by law enforcement officers using the Flock system. And with all those cancellations, Flock has also reportedly offered voluntary employee buyouts as a way to shrink its workforce.

一名联邦法官本周裁定，俄克拉何马州塔尔萨市的一名副警长在未取得搜查令的情况下使用Flock Safety系统检索一名女性的车牌信息，侵犯了该女性在宪法第四修正案下的权利。

正如404 Media所报道的，该裁决并未形成具有约束力的先例，但这属于联邦法官首次认定Flock搜查违宪的案件之一。

在本案中，萨拉·希尔（Sara Hill）法官表示，该副警长在Flock数据库中检索该女性车牌之前本应取得搜查令，因为除了“（该女性的车辆）悬挂加利福尼亚州车牌这一事实”之外，他“没有明显的理由”进行该检索。

随后，该副警长将该女性在Flock系统中的行驶轨迹记录作为搜查其车辆的正当理由之一，并据称在车内发现了91磅冰毒。但希尔法官在裁决书中写道，在Flock搜查之后获得的所有证据“均属于毒树之果，必须予以排除”。

希尔法官还将批评矛头更广泛地指向了对Flock数据库的无令状检索，写道追踪人们的行踪——即使他们身处公共场所——也会“在执法部门能够长期无差别且被动地记录你的行踪，并在任何方便的时候将其用于任何目的时，引发宪法层面的问题”。

“这是一种无差别的群体大规模监控，”希尔写道。“它并非像[卡彭特诉美国案（Carpenter v. United States，最高法院审理的一起关于政府机构如何获取手机位置数据的案件）]中那样针对单个个人。它是一种每时每刻都在收集途经任何联网摄像头的全部车辆信息的工具，并根据执法部门的需求随时提供这些信息。”

希尔加入到了跨越不同政治立场的越来越多对Flock提出批评的人士行列中。包括佛罗里达州和得克萨斯州在内的众多地方和州政府已表示将停止使用该技术。周五，来自佛蒙特州的民主党参议员伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）提出了《阻止Flock法案》（Block Flock Act），该法案将禁止联邦机构使用如Flock之类的自动车牌识别系统。

Flock首席执行官加勒特·兰利（Garrett Langley）——我们将在TechCrunch Disrupt大会的舞台上对他进行采访——此前曾呼吁在隐私与安全之间达成“妥协”，并向那些曾遭到执法人员利用Flock系统进行跟踪的女性道歉。随着众多合作被取消，据报道Flock还提供了自愿买断离职方案以精简员工规模。

aiStories.title: 亚马逊回应数据中心抵制潮，称已不再使用保密协议（NDA）
aiStories.originalTitle: Amazon responds to data center backlash, says it no longer uses NDAs
aiStories.snippet: The CEO of Amazon Web Services tried to push back against widespread suspicion of data centers.
aiStories.fullContent:
Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman said the company has stopped using nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) in its dealings with government agencies as it seeks approval to build new data centers.

Garman’s statement is just one sentence in a longer blog post in which he tried to push back against widespread suspicion of data centers, and to make the case that they’re actually good for communities.

NDAs are a significant piece of the broader data center backlash. For example, environmental activist Erin Brockovich recently said that the number one complaint she’s heard about data centers is transparency, with these projects following a common pattern: “projects announced after permits are already secured, developers who don’t return calls, local officials who signed NDAs before their neighbors knew a project was being considered.”

As a result of that backlash, New York announced a one-year moratorium on permits for large data centers, and according to Garman, there are more than 100 data center moratoriums currently being considered across the United States.

“If these measures are enacted, the U.S. could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations,” Garman claimed. “As a country, we can’t afford to find ourselves in that position.”

Garman also attempted to puncture what he said are four big myths around data centers: that they consume too much water, that they increase electricity costs, that they emit an enormous amount of pollution, and that they don’t provide any benefits to their communities.

Pointing to an Amazon report about its own water usage, Garman said that “direct data center water consumption” only accounts for 0.5% of all industrial water usage in the United States, “orders of magnitude less than golf courses, almond farming, and many other industries.”

Nvidia recently said its new cooling system eliminates “pretty much all water usage” inside the data center, but those claims — like Amazon’s — seem to ignore the broader water usage involved in electricity generation and chip manufacturing. Scientists have also said they need to study data centers’ water and energy usage independently, since there are no federal or state requirements around how tech companies report this data.

As for electricity rates, Garman said they’ve only gone up in some states with large numbers of data centers, while they’ve gone down or at least grown more slowly in others. And he argued, “In instances where energy rates are going up, it’s primarily because the grid is old and hasn’t been invested in and expanded before the demand arrived.”

On the other hand, an independent watchdog said recently data centers were the main culprit behind a 76% year-over-year price increase on America’s largest electrical grid.

When it comes to pollution — an issue that the NAACP is currently suing Elon Musk’s SpaceX/xAI over — Garman complained that critics focus on the maximum amount of pollution allowed under data center permits. For example, a planned Amazon data center in Texas is permitted to release 33 million tons of carbon dioxide per year, which is more than any other power plant in the United States.

“The truth is data center generators almost never run,” Garman said. “They’re idle 99.9% of the time (they run roughly 10 hours per year, mostly for required maintenance testing).”

As for the community benefits, this is where Garman wrote, “We no longer use nondisclosure agreements with the government agencies we work with on our projects.” Plus, he said, “Over the past three years, Amazon has contributed more than $1 billion to communities across the U.S. in which we have a meaningful data center presence.”

Will this be enough to quell community suspicion? Perhaps not — Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently argued that the AI backlash is “fundamentally a crisis of trust,” where people assume governments and tech companies are always “cooking up some new way to screw them over.” Similarly, writer Jasmine Sun noted that when data center opponents are presented with the tech companies’ arguments, their response is usually, “I don’t believe them.”

亚马逊云科技（Amazon Web Services，AWS）首席执行官马特·加曼（Matt Garman）表示，该公司在寻求批准建设新数据中心时，已停止在与政府机构的往来中使用保密协议（NDA）。

加曼的这一表态出自一篇较长博文中的一句话。他在文中试图回击外界对数据中心普遍存在的疑虑，并论证数据中心实际上对当地社区有益。

保密协议是更广泛的数据中心抵制潮中的关键焦点之一。例如，环保活动人士埃琳·布罗克维奇（Erin Brockovich）最近表示，她听到的关于数据中心的第一大抱怨就是透明度问题，这些项目普遍遵循一种套路：“在获得许可证后才宣布项目、开发商拒不回电、地方官员在邻居们根本不知道项目正在审议前就已经签署了保密协议。”

受此类抵制的影响，纽约州宣布对大型数据中心审批实施为期一年的暂缓令；据加曼称，目前全美有超过100项数据中心暂缓令正在审议中。

“如果这些措施得以实施，美国可能正在亲手写下输掉这场竞赛的败局，其后果将延续几代人，”加曼坚称，“作为一个国家，我们承受不起陷入这种境地的代价。”

加曼还试图破除他所称的围绕数据中心的“四大误区”：消耗过多水资源、推高电费、排放大量污染物，以及未给当地社区带来任何益处。

加曼援引亚马逊自身用水报告指出，“直接数据中心用水量”仅占美国所有工业用水量的0.5%，“比高尔夫球场、杏仁种植以及许多其他行业低了几个数量级”。

英伟达（Nvidia）最近表示其全新冷却系统消除了数据中心内部“几乎所有的水资源使用”，但这些言论——就像亚马逊的说法一样——似乎忽略了发电和芯片制造过程中涉及的更广泛用水。科学家们也表示，鉴于联邦或州层面并未对科技公司如何报告此类数据作出强制要求，他们需要对数据中心的水资源和能源消耗进行独立研究。

至于电费问题，加曼表示，电费仅在部分拥有大量数据中心的州有所上涨，而在其他州则有所下降，或至少涨幅较为平缓。他辩称：“在能源价格上涨的情况下，主要是因为电网老旧，在需求激增之前未能获得足够的投资与扩建。”

然而另一方面，一家独立监管机构最近表示，数据中心是美国最大电网电价同比上涨76%的主要元凶。

谈及污染问题——美国全国有色人种协进会（NAACP）目前正就此问题起诉埃隆·马斯克的SpaceX/xAI——加曼抱怨批评者总是紧盯着数据中心许可证所允许的最大排污量。例如，亚马逊计划在得克萨斯州建设的一座数据中心获准每年排放3300万吨二氧化碳，这一规模超过了美国任何一座发电厂。

“事实是，数据中心的发电机几乎从不运行，”加曼说，“它们99.9%的时间都处于闲置状态（每年大约只运行10小时，主要用于合规维护测试）。”

关于社区福祉，加曼正是写道：“在与我们项目合作的政府机构中，我们不再使用保密协议。”此外，他表示：“在过去三年中，亚马逊已向我们在美开展重大数据中心业务的各个社区捐款超过10亿美元。”

这是否足以平息社区的猜疑？也许并不能——Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪（Dario Amodei）最近指出，围绕人工智能的抵制“从根本上说是一场信任危机”，人们总是认为政府和科技公司在“暗中酝酿某种坑害他们的新手段”。同样，作家贾斯敏·孙（Jasmine Sun）指出，当数据中心的反对者面对科技公司的论据时，他们的反应通常只是：“我才不信他们。”

During a presentation on the future of RE Engine, Capcom laid out its plans to embrace AI in ‘development workflows.’

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

Capcom’s Pragmata might be all about the horrors of AI, but in practice the studio doesn’t seem so down on the tech. During the Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026 programmer Satoshi Ishida gave a presentation with the mouthful of a title: “The Outlook and Future of the REX Project, Further Evolving the RE Engine for the Next Generation.” During the talk he laid out the challenges facing studios producing games at the scale of Resident Evil, which can make even simple tasks extremely time consuming. The solution Ishida said is “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows.”

Capcom has said previously that it will not use AI-generated assets in its games, and instead would focus on using the tech to make development more efficient. Ishida’s comments seem to lineup, though definitely seem to leave the door open to more extensive use. He laid out a plan to turn RE Engine slowly, and incrementally, into an “AI-generation game engine” building towards a “a future where we create games together with AI,” according to IGN’s translation.

Capcom此前曾表示，不会在游戏中使用AI生成的素材资产，而是专注于利用该技术提升开发效率。石田的言论看似与此前表态一致，但显然也为更广泛的应用留出了可能性。据IGN的译文，他提出了一项计划，旨在循序渐进地将RE引擎改造成“AI世代游戏引擎”，逐步迈向“与AI共同制作游戏的未来”。

aiStories.title: OpenAI安全团队员工辞职，直指公司“文化已然崩坏”
aiStories.originalTitle: OpenAI safety employee resigns, claiming the company’s ‘culture is broken’
aiStories.snippet: By his own admission, David Robinson is “something of a cliché”: an employee at a leading AI company who issues a dire warning while resigning from their job.
aiStories.fullContent:
By his own admission, David Robinson is “something of a cliché”: an employee at a leading AI company who issues a dire warning while resigning from their job.

In an essay published in The Atlantic, Robinson said he led the writing of safety reports that accompanied OpenAI’s major product launches. He also said that with three-and-a-half years at OpenAI, he is “among the longest-tenured employees at the company.” Now he’s quitting, because in his view, the company’s “culture is broken.”

In some ways, Robinson’s comments echo those of Jacob Coxon, who worked as a researcher at both OpenAI and Anthropic before quitting and declaring that these companies are “gambling with our lives.” Coxon’s comments led to a broader debate about AI safety, with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei unveiling a plan for more cautious AI development; AI executives met with President Donald Trump this week and signed what appeared to be hastily written, non-binding pledge to implement more safety controls.

But in Robinson’s view, the debate needs to go beyond “specific rules or new laws,” addressing the overall culture at these companies. And while much of the reporting around OpenAI has focused on how the company’s CEO Sam Altman lost the trust of former colleagues, Robinson’s essay suggests that OpenAI’s culture issues are the same as those of Silicon Valley at large.

“OpenAI has thrived by trial and error (which it calls ‘iterative deployment’), looking for problems and improving its guardrails in response,” he wrote. “But this approach, by its very nature, guarantees periodic failures — and the scale of those failures is growing as systems get more capable.”

Pointing to the recent breach of Hugging Face systems by OpenAI agents, as well as continuing revelations of OpenAI discovering more rogue agents, Robinson argued, “An environment where things like this can happen is no place to grow artificial minds that could be smarter than we are and that might not do what we want them to.”

Given the increased risk, Robinson argued that frontier AI companies need to start operating “like nuclear-power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster.”

But Robinson said that in his time at OpenAI, he “never encountered a colleague who had experience making airplanes fly safely or nuclear reactors run without melting down, or helping the financial system grow without collapsing.”

In response to Robinson’s essay, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company continues to improve its safety measures.

“We’re making sure our models don’t become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down,” Pusateri said in a statement. “We’re making significant changes to strengthen security in our research and testing environments, train models to not just complete tasks but do so responsibly, expand our work with third-party evaluators, and improve real-time monitoring so we can detect and respond to concerning behavior earlier in the training process.”

Beyond calling for changes in OpenAI’s culture, Robinson also said it’s time to ask bigger questions about alignment — something that he admitted could sound “touchy-feely,” but he said it’s critical as companies’ current “measures of how well” AI systems “match human values are coarse.”

“The smarter the industry lets models grow while these problems remain unsolved, the more dangerous our situation becomes,” he said.

Robinson’s departure was first reported by Business Insider. In his essay, he also acknowledged that he’s following an apparently a common step in the AI whistleblower playbook: He’s hired a PR firm. But he insisted, “The decision to speak out is mine alone.”

“Perhaps I should have stayed and fought for fundamental shifts in our staffing and culture, but in practice, my colleagues and I were so busy sprinting that we seldom had the chance to consider big changes, much less to actually make them,” Robinson said. “That’s why I concluded that stronger incentives for safety — coming from outside the company — are a big part of getting this right.”

大卫·罗宾逊（David Robinson）坦言，自己成了“某种老生常谈的典型”：作为一家顶尖人工智能公司的员工，在辞职的同时发出了严厉警告。

在《大西洋月刊》（The Atlantic）发表的一篇文章中，罗宾逊表示，他曾负责主笔撰写伴随OpenAI重大产品发布的安全报告。他还提到，自己在OpenAI工作了三年半，“是公司工龄最长的员工之一”。如今他选择辞职，因为在他看来，公司的“文化已经崩坏”。

在某些方面，罗宾逊的言论呼应了雅各布·考克森（Jacob Coxon）的观点。考克森曾先后在OpenAI和Anthropic担任研究员，辞职时他宣称这些公司“拿我们的性命做赌注”。考克森的言论引发了关于人工智能安全的更广泛辩论，促使Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）公布了一项更加谨慎的AI发展计划；此外，AI领域的高管们本周与唐纳德·特朗普总统会面，并签署了一份看似仓促草就、不具约束力的协议，承诺实施更多安全管控措施。

但在罗宾逊看来，这场辩论需要超越“具体的规则或新法律”，直面这些公司的整体文化。尽管围绕OpenAI的大量报道都聚焦于公司首席执行官萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）如何失去了前同事的信任，但罗宾逊的文章指出，OpenAI的文化问题与整个硅谷如出一辙。

他写道：“OpenAI通过试错（它称之为‘迭代部署’）蓬勃发展，寻找问题并据此改进安全护栏。但这种方式从本质上就注定了阶段性的失败——而且随着系统能力的增强，这些失败的规模也在不断扩大。”

针对近期OpenAI智能体入侵Hugging Face系统事件，以及OpenAI不断曝出发现更多失控智能体的情况，罗宾逊指出：“能发生这类事情的环境，绝不是培育可能比我们更聪明、且可能不按我们意愿行事的‘人工头脑’的场所。”

考虑到不断增加的风险，罗宾逊认为，前沿AI公司需要开始像“核电站或繁忙的机场那样运营，设置层层冗余，并进行周密、耗时的规划，以确保偶尔且不可避免的人为失误不会引向灾难之门”。

但罗宾逊表示，在OpenAI任职期间，他“从未遇到过有保障飞机安全飞行、核反应堆无熔毁运转，或帮助金融系统持续增长而不崩溃等经验的同事”。

针对罗宾逊的文章，OpenAI发言人德鲁·普萨泰里（Drew Pusateri）表示，公司一直在持续改进其安全措施。

普萨泰里在一份声明中表示：“我们正在确保我们的模型不会超越我们所能安全管理与保障的能力范畴，当需要放缓步伐时，我们会暂停训练或暂缓推出模型。我们正在进行重大调整，以增强研究与测试环境中的安全性，训练模型不仅要完成任务，而且要负责任地完成任务，扩大与第三方评估机构的合作，并改善实时监控，以便我们在训练过程的早期发现并应对令人担忧的行为。”

除了呼吁改变OpenAI的文化之外，罗宾逊还表示，现在是时候就对齐问题（alignment）提出更重大的疑问了——他坦承这听起来可能有点“流于感性”，但他表示这至关重要，因为目前各家公司衡量AI系统“契合人类价值观程度的标准十分粗糙”。

他说：“在这些问题尚未解决的情况下，行业放任模型变得越聪明，我们的处境就会越危险。”

罗宾逊的离职最早由《商业内幕》（Business Insider）报道。在他的文章中，他也承认自己遵循了AI吹哨人常规剧本中的一步：他聘请了一家公关公司。但他坚称：“公开发声的决定完全由我个人做出。”

罗宾逊说：“也许我本应该留下来，为我们的人员配置和文化争取根本性的转变，但在实际工作中，我和同事们都忙于向前冲刺，极少有机会去思考重大变革，更不用说真正去实施了。这就是为什么我得出结论：来自公司外部更强大的安全激励措施，是解决这一问题的关键部分。”

aiStories.fullContent:
It’s not even October yet and Amazon is already offering some Prime Big Deal Day discounts on its own hardware, along with plenty of other popular products. It’s all to hype up October Prime Day , which starts October 6th at 3AM ET and lasts through 3AM ET on the 8th if you’re on the East Coast (12AM PT).

October Prime Day offers a glimpse of deals that will likely be available again during Black Friday and Cyber Monday. So, with the holiday shopping season officially underway, you can get some of your shopping out of the way before things get busier as we approach the holidays.

The most recent update to this post on October 3rd added a couple of Bose speakers, building on what was added on October 1st (a couple of Belkin deals, plus a discount on a capable 1440p USB-C monitor). This post will be updated ahead of October 6th as new deals become available.

While the Max is an awesome, powerful speaker, the Plus packs a ton of performance into a more portable form factor. It has an IP67 rating, and it’s easy to clean, too. Read our review .

$269 $179 at Best Buy

Bose’s SoundLink Max improves on the smaller Flex with true stereo sound — and very powerful sound at that. It’s got a removable handle for easy transport, and there’s an aux input for playing audio when you want to listen at a higher quality than what Bluetooth can deliver. Read our review .

$399 $279 at Best Buy

Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 foldable charging dock

Slap a recent iPhone onto this charging pad and it’ll charge at fast 25W speeds. It can also charge AirPods, and includes a cord and wall adapter.

$100 $75 at Amazon (w/ Apple Watch support)

Belkin Charging Case for Nintendo Switch 2

The case features an integrated power bank and a small pocket to stow an AirTag (or other similarly sized Bluetooth tracker).

$69.99 $59.49 at Amazon (in black or sand)

Asus ProArt 27-inch 1440p USB-C monitor

An affordable color-accurate monitor that can easily connect to a MacBook or Windows machine that has USB-C video support. It’s a good price for a fully-featured 1440p monitor.

Belkin MagSafe 15W 2-in-1 wireless charging dock

A slick 2-in-1 charger that can charge your magnet-friendly iPhone or Pixel at a relatively speedy pace. Its extra charging pad supports AirPods, the Apple Watch, and other Qi-ready accessories.

$120 $59.99 at Amazon

Ring Battery Doorbell 2K

At more than half-off, the second-gen version is a good deal if you want 2K video and easy installation. However, its battery is built-in, so you’ll need to disconnect the doorbell to charge via USB-C.

$99.99 $39.99 at Amazon

$99.99 $39.99 at Best Buy

Bissell ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus carpet cleaner

Bissell’s Little Green is handy, but doesn’t cut it for big jobs. If you have pets and a lot of carpet to clean, this is one of the most powerful upright carpet cleaners in its price range.

$279.99 $209.99 at Amazon

$279.99 $209.99 at Bissell

Ring Floodlight Cam 2K

This model requires wired power, and provides 2K resolution (with AI tuning) and 6x digital zoom. It’s bright (2,000 lumens), and provides a loud alarm if you need to use it.

$199.99 $99.99 at Amazon

Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro

The highest-end battery-powered option of the lineup. It can record in 4K with 10x digital zoom, and its battery can be swapped for another as it recharges.

$249.99 $149.99 at Amazon

$249.99 $149.99 at Best Buy

Amazon Fire HD 8 tablet

The eight-inch tablet with lockscreen ads has 4GB RAM (respectable for streaming apps and mobile games), plus 64GB of storage and a microSD slot for viewing locally-stored media. This model doesn’t support Google Play Store, though it’s easy to sideload it.

$129.99 $79.99 at Amazon (4GB RAM, 64GB)

$99.99 $54.99 at Best Buy (3GB RAM, 32GB)

Ecovacs Deebot X12 OmniCyclone

The X12 OmniCyclone uses AI to identify and blast stains to help ensure they’re properly cleaned with minimal passes. It includes a dock, which empties the vac, washes its rolling mop with heated, pressurized water, and refills its reservoirs.

$1499.99 $799 at Amazon

$1499.99 $841.99 at Best Buy

$1499.99 $842 at Ecovacs

Blink Mini pan and tilt camera

The panning and tilting accessory gives the Blink Mini some new powers, including 360-degree control via the Blink app. Also included is the camera, which is usually $25 by itself.

$39.99 $23.99 at Amazon

$39.99 $23.99 at Best Buy

Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus

The latest version of Amazon’s zippy Fire TV Stick 4K streams in 4K resolution, as its name suggests, and features support for Wi-Fi 6, Dolby Atmos / Vision, and HDR10 Plus.

$69.99 $37.99 at Amazon

$69.99 $37.99 at Best Buy

Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2023, latest model)

Amazon’s highest-end streaming stick supports Wi-Fi 6E and offers double the storage of its predecessor. It also displays widgets and artwork when idle, while continuing to offer a terrific selection of streaming apps. Plus, it runs on the new and improved Fire TV OS, which makes it easier to find something to watch.

$84.99 $44.99 at Amazon

$84.99 $44.99 at Best Buy

Amazon Fire TV Cube (2022, latest model)

The hybrid Echo and Fire TV is faster than its predecessor with extensive hands-free voice control capabilities, support for Wi-Fi 6E, and excellent performance. Read our review .

$199.99 $89.99 at Amazon

$199.99 $89.99 at Best Buy

Amazon’s smart speaker-meets-alarm clock has a 2.83-inch squared-off display for showing the time, weather, album art, and other bits of info you may want at your bedside. Unlike the original, there’s no camera to worry about having in your bedroom — though it does have a mutable mic for Alexa voice controls. Read our review.

$109.99 $54.99 at Amazon

$109.99 $54.99 at Best Buy

$109.99 $54.99 at Target

The Echo Dot Max is an elegant redesign of Amazon’s orb-shaped smart speaker, with high-quality knit fabric, a flat face, a new LED ring, and touch controls. It’s the first Echo Dot with Amazon’s improved two-way speaker system and support for its new AI-powered assistant, Alexa Plus, which is enabled out of the box.

$119.99 $79.99 at Amazon

$119.99 $79.99 at Best Buy

$119.99 $79.99 at Target

Amazon Echo Dot (Fifth-Gen)

Amazon’s Echo Dot is an affordable way to add a smart speaker to your space. The small, powerful speaker offers surprisingly robust sound, and it’s great for controlling smart home devices, including those compatible with Matter. The Dot also offers faster response times than its predecessor, and it can act as an extender for an Eero Wi-Fi system. Read our review .

$79.99 $39.99 at Amazon

$79.99 $39.99 at Best Buy

$79.99 $39.99 at Target

Amazon Echo Show 11 (2025)

The Echo Show 11 features an 11-inch screen and 1080p resolution. It includes Alexa Plus and can be used as a smart home hub with support Thread, Matter, and Zigbee smart home protocols. Read our review.

$249.99 $149.99 at Amazon

$249.99 $149.99 at Best Buy

$249.99 $149.99 at Target

The new year is the perfect time to reset your routines and get organized, and the Echo Show 15 is a great tool for doing just that. Designed to function as a shared household hub, it keeps calendars, schedules, reminders, to-do lists, and notes visible at a glance, making it easier to keep on top of things. As an Alexa-enabled smart display, you can also add events by voice and control compatible smart home devices.

$349.99 $249.99 at Amazon

$349.99 $249.99 at Best Buy

$349.99 $249.99 at Target

Eero Pro 6E tri-band router

Eero’s Pro 6E mesh router is the Amazon-owned company’s last-gen model. It supports the 6GHz Wi-Fi band with speeds of up to 1.3Gbps and covers up to 2,000 square feet with one unit. Wired speeds can go up to 2.5Gbps. Read our review .

$199.99 $149.99 at Amazon (single pack)

$499.99 $374.99 at Best Buy (three-pack)

$499.99 $374.99 at Amazon (three-pack)

Samsung 32-inch Movingstyle smart display

Similar to LG’s rollable StanbyME display, the Movingstyle Essential is a 32-inch 4K display on a base that’s height-adjustable (and supports swiveling, pivoting and tilting). Unlike LG’s model, though, this one has no built-in battery.

$699.99 $499.99 at Amazon

With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum and mop hybrid.

$1099.99 $899.99 at Amazon (for Prime members)

$1099.99 $849.99 at Dreame (with free account)

10月Prime会员日让人们得以提前一窥可能在“黑色星期五”和“网络星期一”期间再次出现的优惠。因此，随着假日购物季正式拉开帷幕，您可以在临近节日变得更加忙碌之前，提前搞定一部分购物需求。

本文于10月3日的最新更新增加了几款Bose音箱，这是在10月1日新增内容（包括几项贝尔金优惠以及一款性能出色的1440p USB-C显示器折扣）基础上的补充。随着更多新优惠的推出，本文将在10月6日之前持续更新。

虽然Max是一款功能强大且出色的音箱，但Plus则将强劲的性能融入到了更便携的机身之中。它具备IP67级防尘防水认证，而且非常易于清洁。阅读我们的评测。

百思买售价：179美元（原价269美元）

Bose的SoundLink Max在体型更小的Flex基础上进行了升级，带来了真正的立体声音效——而且声音极其震撼。它配有可拆卸手柄便于携带，并提供了一个AUX音频输入接口，方便你在追求比蓝牙传输更高音质时播放音频。阅读我们的评测。

百思买售价：279美元（原价399美元）

贝尔金（Belkin）Qi2.2 25W二合一折叠无线充电底座

只需将近期的iPhone吸附在这款充电板上，即可实现高达25W的快速充电。它还能为AirPods充电，并附带充电线和充电头。

亚马逊售价：75美元（原价100美元，支持Apple Watch）

贝尔金任天堂Switch 2充电保护盒

亚马逊售价：59.49美元（原价69.99美元，有黑色或沙色可选）

华硕（Asus）ProArt 27英寸1440p USB-C显示器

一款性价比极高的专业色彩显示器，可轻松连接至支持USB-C视频输出的MacBook或Windows电脑。对于一台功能完备的1440p显示器而言，这个价格非常划算。

一款外观小巧时尚的二合一充电器，能够以较快速度为支持磁吸的iPhone或Pixel手机充电。其额外的充电板还支持AirPods、Apple Watch以及其他兼容Qi标准的配件。

亚马逊售价：59.99美元（原价120美元）

Ring电池版2K智能门铃

亚马逊售价：39.99美元（原价99.99美元）
百思买售价：39.99美元（原价99.99美元）

亚马逊售价：99.99美元（原价199.99美元）

Ring 4K Pro电池版智能门铃

X12 OmniCyclone利用AI识别并强力去除污渍，确保以最少的清扫次数达到理想的清洁效果。它配备全能基站，可自动集尘、使用加压热水清洗滚筒拖布，并为主机自动补水。

Blink Mini云台监控摄像头

亚马逊售价：23.99美元（原价39.99美元）
百思买售价：23.99美元（原价39.99美元）

亚马逊Fire TV Stick 4K Plus电视棒

亚马逊最新款的高速Fire TV Stick 4K正如其名称所示支持4K超高清流媒体播放，并支持Wi-Fi 6、杜比全景声（Dolby Atmos）、杜比视界（Dolby Vision）和HDR10+。

百思买售价：37.99美元（原价69.99美元）

aiStories.title: 受政府命令影响，杰克·多西旗下的 Bitchat 在印度从各应用商店下架
aiStories.originalTitle: Jack Dorsey’s Bitchat disappears from app stores in India after government order
aiStories.snippet: Bitchat has become largely unavailable in India as a result of the restrictions.
aiStories.fullContent:
Bitchat, Jack Dorsey’s decentralized messaging app designed to work without an internet connection, has disappeared from Apple and Google’s app stores in India, months after New Delhi first sought to restrict access to the open-source software.

Dorsey said Saturday that the Indian government had ordered Apple to remove Bitchat from its App Store in the country. In a notice from Apple that Dorsey posted on X, India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued the demand under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, the country’s primary legal provision for government-ordered online blocking.

Apple’s notice said Bitchat would remain available on its App Store outside India. However, access to the app through its TestFlight beta-testing service would also be blocked in the country.

Bitchat was also no longer available for download through Google Play in India when TechCrunch checked on Saturday. Bitchat’s website was also inaccessible across various internet service providers in the country. It was not immediately clear whether Google and internet service providers had also received directions from the federal government.

Apple, Google, and India’s IT ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

Launched in July last year, Bitchat uses Bluetooth mesh networking to allow nearby devices to exchange encrypted messages without relying on cellular networks, internet access, or centralized servers.

In July 2026, Dorsey revealed that Indian authorities had ordered GitHub to take down repositories associated with the open-source messaging app, raising questions among digital rights advocates and legal experts about the legal basis for restricting software based on its functionality.

The Indian government said in its order to GitHub at the time that Bitchat’s architecture made it hard for law enforcement agencies to intercept communications or trace users, and pointed to its ability to continue operating during internet shutdowns. The July order relied on a provision of India’s information technology law that deals with intermediaries and their liability for third-party content. That differs from Section 69A, cited in Apple’s latest notice.

The Internet Freedom Foundation, a New Delhi-based digital rights advocacy group, called the latest order unconstitutional, arguing that Section 69A allows the government to block unlawful information but not a messaging app because of its ability to operate during internet shutdowns. It also said neither the blocking order nor the allegedly illegal content cited as the basis for the action had been made public.

The latest restrictions on Bitchat come as India is seeing a fresh wave of ⁠youth-led protests over changes to the country’s voter rolls. Police detained several people during demonstrations in New Delhi on Saturday, as protesters demanded the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner over alleged manipulation of electoral rolls. Authorities suspended internet services around New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar for 12 hours on Friday during protests there.

During July’s protests, demonstrators reportedly turned to Bitchat and rival app Briar after authorities suspended internet services.

Interest in Bitchat surged in India around the same time. The country accounted for about 85% of the app’s global downloads between July 17 and July 23, up from roughly 1% in the previous 30 days, data from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower showed.

杰克·多西（Jack Dorsey）旗下的去中心化通讯应用 Bitchat（该应用旨在无需互联网连接即可运行）已从苹果和谷歌在印度的应用商店中下架。数月前，新德里方面首次试图限制对这款开源软件的访问。

多西周六表示，印度政府已命令苹果公司将其应用商店（App Store）中的 Bitchat 在该国下架。多西在 X 平台上发布了苹果公司发来的一份通知，印度电子和信息技术部依据《信息技术法》第 69A 条发出了该要求，该条款是印度政府下令实施网络封锁的主要法律依据。

苹果公司的通知指出，Bitchat 在印度以外地区的 App Store 中仍可正常下载使用。不过，通过其 TestFlight 测试服务访问该应用的操作也将在该国遭到封锁。

TechCrunch 在周六核实发现，印度用户同样无法再通过 Google Play 下载 Bitchat。此外，通过印度境内的多家互联网服务提供商也无法访问 Bitchat 的官方网站。目前尚不清楚谷歌和各互联网服务提供商是否也收到了来自联邦政府的指示。

苹果、谷歌以及印度电子和信息技术部均未回应置评请求。

Bitchat 于去年 7 月推出，它利用蓝牙网状网络（Bluetooth mesh networking），让附近设备在无需依赖蜂窝网络、互联网访问或中心化服务器的情况下互发加密信息。

2026 年 7 月，多西披露印度当局已下令 GitHub 下架与这款开源通讯应用相关的代码仓库，这引发了数字权利倡导人士和法律专家对于仅凭软件功能就予以限制的做法是否具有法律依据的质疑。

印度政府在当时发给 GitHub 的命令中称，Bitchat 的架构使执法机构难以拦截通信或追踪用户，并指出该应用具备在断网期间继续运行的能力。7 月份的这份命令依据的是印度信息技术法中关于中介机构及其对第三方内容责任的规定。这与苹果最新通知中引用的第 69A 条有所不同。

总部位于新德里的数字权利倡导组织“互联网自由基金会”（Internet Freedom Foundation）称最新的这一命令违宪，认为第 69A 条仅允许政府封锁非法信息，而不能仅仅因为一款通讯应用具备在断网期间运行的能力就对其进行封锁。该组织还表示，无论是封锁令本身，还是作为采取行动依据的涉嫌违法内容，均未对外公开。

对 Bitchat 的最新限制出台之际，印度正因选民名册变动而掀起新一波由青年主导的抗议浪潮。抗议者指控选举名册遭到操纵，并要求印度首席选举专员辞职，警方在周六于新德里举行的示威活动中拘留了数人。周五，当局在新德里简塔·曼塔天文台（Jantar Mantar）周边抗议期间，对该区域切断网络服务达 12 小时。

据报道，在 7 月的抗议活动中，由于当局切断了网络服务，示威者纷纷转向使用 Bitchat 和竞品应用 Briar。

与此同时，印度国内对 Bitchat 的关注度出现激增。市场情报机构 Sensor Tower 的数据显示，在 7 月 17 日至 7 月 23 日期间，印度占该应用全球下载量的约 85%，而在此前 30 天内这一比例仅为约 1%。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All Entertainment

As head of Splice, Kakul has tried to carefully thread the line on AI music tools. She also hates her cup warmer.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Kakul Srivastava is the CEO of Splice, the sample platform countless producers rely on for one-shots and melodic loops. Samples pulled from the service have found their way into massive hits like Lisa’s “Money” and “Espresso” by Sabrina Carpenter. (The original samples are here and here, for the curious.)

Before that, Kakul held executive roles at Flickr, Yahoo, GitHub, and Adobe. Throughout her career, Kakul has found herself at the intersection of Silicon Valley and creatives. That’s been especially true at Splice, where she’s not just expanded the platform’s footprint by acquiring Spitfire Audio, but also overseen its forays into the world of generative AI.

Last year, she was very outspoken on an episode of Decoder about avoiding the sort of “push-button, get-song” AI that has made companies like Suno so controversial. And based on her answers to our questionnaire, it doesn’t seem like her skepticism has waned. When it comes to Splice, the company has made a point of trying to offer AI products that still keep the human at the center of the creative process. And when it comes to communicating with colleagues, Kakul sees the same need to keep AI at bay.

What is your most indispensable tool?

A well-written document and a real conversation about it.

Splice is remote-first, so we don’t have a hallway. What we have instead is somebody sitting down and actually thinking something through, and then a bunch of people arguing with it. Almost everything good that’s happened here started that way.

Which is why I’m careful about AI-written documents. Once you can’t tell whether there’s a person behind the words, the conversation you have about it becomes a different conversation, and a worse one. And you can’t really go back from that. I think the same thing is true of music.

What is your happy place online?

Instagram, which I know is not the fashionable answer. My feed has turned into almost entirely people making music in ways I would never have thought of. There’s gothic western, which I did not know was a thing. There’s a woman in Russia who organizes street dancing. There’s a guy playing modern hits on a hammered dulcimer. The Indian chai-wala rapping. I could watch it all, all day.

What game do you have the fondest memories of?

Antakshari. It’s an Indian game — you sing a bit of a song, and whatever letter the line ends on is the letter the next person has to start their song with. You play it on long car rides, at weddings, any time a group of people is stuck somewhere together.

I love that the whole game is made out of music and none of the players are musicians. You just have to remember, and you have to be willing to sing in front of your family, which for most people is the harder part. And then when you watch people’s faces get soft when the song really hits — even when it’s sung badly. That’s the power of music.

What’s the most disappointing gadget you’ve owned?

A cup warmer. It warms the cup. It does not warm the coffee. I want to be clear that it works exactly as designed.

What creation are you most proud of?

I can’t not say my kids. Watching a person go from nothing to a fully formed human with opinions you did not give them is the most amazing thing I have been anywhere near. And the strange part is that it isn’t rare. It’s happening in every house on the street. We all just watch it happen and then go about our day.

Which are you least proud of?

I was on the early team at Tiny Speck, the company that later became Slack. Before Slack, we made a game called Glitch — a massively multiplayer open world — and it was one of the most beautiful things I’ve ever worked on. The art, the sound, the writing, the way the world actually worked. Some of the most talented people I’ve ever been around.

It failed, and it failed for reasons that were sitting right there in front of us. It was built on Flash, and Adobe had already stopped investing in Flash. It was a PC experience at the exact moment the whole world was moving to playing games on a phone. Two enormous tectonic trends, and we didn’t account for either one in time to do anything about them. I feel like I let down the creativity of the people who built something beautiful.

What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?

Say the thing, then explain it. Don’t lay all your proof out first, hoping it earns you the right to make your point. Nobody is listening to the proof yet. They’re listening for whether you sound like you believe it. The confidence you say it with is what makes room for the explanation.

What is your current obsession?

Cooking my mother’s food. She died before I learned most of it from her, so I’ve been reconstructing her recipes off YouTube — strangers in their own kitchens, making the thing the way their mothers made it. It takes a lot of tries. I got one of them right last year, and the taste put me straight back to being eight years old with my mom by my side.

This is what I think about when people ask me what technology is for. Some guy uploaded a video of his family’s recipe and gave me my mother’s cooking back. He will never know that.

What do you think is worth splurging on?

Live jazz. There is nothing else like being in a room where people are making decisions in real time and can’t take them back. I travel a lot for work, and if there’s any way to get to a show in whatever city I’m in, I’ll do it, even when it means I’m useless the next morning.

What would the tagline for your biopic be?

A heist movie where nothing gets stolen and everybody gets paid.

What’s the last GIF or meme you used?

卡库尔·斯里瓦斯塔瓦（Kakul Srivastava）是Splice的首席执行官。无数制作人都依赖这个音频采样平台获取单发采样（one-shots）与旋律循环片段（melodic loops）。该平台上的音频采样曾被用于众多大热单曲，例如Lisa的《Money》和萨布丽娜·卡彭特（Sabrina Carpenter）的《Espresso》。（感兴趣的读者可以在这里和这里找到原始采样片段。）

在此之前，卡库尔曾先后在Flickr、雅虎、GitHub和Adobe担任高管职务。在她的整个职业生涯中，卡库尔始终身处硅谷与创意人士的交汇点。在Splice尤其如此——她不仅通过收购Spitfire Audio扩大了平台的版图，还亲自操刀引领其迈向生成式AI领域。

去年，她在播客节目《Decoder》中直言不讳地表示，要避免走向“按个按钮就出首歌”的那种AI模式——正是这种模式让Suno等公司备受争议。从她对我们调查问卷的回答来看，她的这种审慎与怀疑态度丝毫未减。在Splice，公司一直坚持提供仍以人类为创意核心的AI产品。而在与同事沟通时，卡库尔同样认为有必要与AI保持距离。

你最不可或缺的工具是什么？
一份撰写精良的文档，以及围绕它展开的真实对话。
Splice推行远程优先办公，所以我们没有茶水间或走廊可以闲聊。取而代之的是，某个人坐下来认真把一件事想透，然后一群人围绕它进行辩论与争论。我们这里几乎所有美好的成果，都是以这种方式诞生的。
这也是为什么我对AI撰写的文档保持警惕。一旦你无法确定文字背后是否有真人在思考，围绕它展开的对话就会变味，变得更糟糕。而那一步一旦跨出，你就很难再回头了。我认为音乐也是同一个道理。

你在网络上的快乐源泉是什么？
Instagram，我知道这算不上什么时髦的答案。我的信息流现在几乎全是人们用我想都想不到的方式做音乐的内容。有我以前闻所未闻的“哥特西部风”（gothic western）；有一位在俄罗斯组织街舞的女士；有一个人用扬琴演奏现代流行金曲；还有印度街头卖奶茶的小哥在说唱。我能津津有味地看上一整天。

你记忆最深的游戏是什么？
安塔克夏里（Antakshari）。这是一个印度传统游戏——你唱出一小段歌，最后一个歌词的发音字母，就是下一位玩家接唱歌曲的开头字母。在漫长的车程中、婚礼上，或者任何一群人被困在一起无事可做的时候，大家都会玩这个。
我喜欢这个游戏完全由音乐构成，而参与者却无一人是专业音乐人。你只需要去回忆，并且愿意当着家人的面放声歌唱——对大多数人来说，后一点才是更难的部分。然后，当你看到某首歌真正打动人心时，人们的表情变得温柔柔和——哪怕那首歌唱得跑调走音。这就是音乐的力量。

你买过最令人失望的科技数码小配件是什么？
一个暖杯垫。它把杯子热得滚烫，却根本热不到咖啡。不过我想说明的是，它的实际表现确实和设计完全一致。

你最引以为傲的创造是什么？
我不能不提我的孩子们。看着一个人从无到有，长成一个拥有自己独立见解的健全的人，而那些想法甚至不是你灌输给他们的，这是我所经历过的最神奇的事情。奇妙的是，这并不罕见。整条街上的每家每户都在发生着同样的事。我们都只是目睹着这一切发生，然后继续过着各自的日常生活。

你最不引以为傲的事情是什么？
我曾是Tiny Speck的早期团队成员，这家公司后来演变成了Slack。在做Slack之前，我们开发了一款名为《Glitch》的游戏——一个大型多人开放世界游戏，那是我参与过的最美妙的作品之一。无论是美术、声效、文案，还是这个虚拟世界的运作机制，全都出自一群我所接触过的最具才华的人之手。
但它失败了，而且失败的原因就摆在眼前。它是基于Flash开发的，而当时Adobe已经停止对Flash的投入；它是一款PC端游戏体验，而彼时整个世界正在全面转向手机游戏。两大翻天覆地的时代趋势，我们却都没有及时考虑到并采取应对措施。我觉得自己辜负了那些创造出如此美好事物的人的才华与创造力。

你听过最好的一条建议是什么？
先抛出核心观点，再去作解释。不要先摆出一堆论据，指望通过它们来赢得陈述观点的权利。那时候根本没人会在意你的论据；大家在听的是，你的语气是否听起来坚信不疑。你表达时的笃定与自信，才会为接下来的阐释留出空间。

你目前最着迷的事情是什么？
做我母亲做过的菜。在她把大部分手艺传给我之前就离世了，所以我一直在通过YouTube复刻她的食谱——看世界各地素不相识的人在自家的厨房里，按照各自母亲的做法烹饪。这需要反复尝试。去年我终于做对了一道，那个味道瞬间让我回到了八岁时依偎在母亲身边的时光。
当别人问我科技的意义何在时，我心里想到的就是这件事。某个陌生人上传了自己家族食谱的视频，却帮我找回了母亲的味道。而他可能永远都不会知道这一点。

你认为什么事情值得挥金如土？
现场爵士乐。那种大家在同一个空间里实时做决定且毫无退路的现场感，是无可替代的。我经常因公出差，无论身在哪座城市，只要有机会能赶去现场听一场演出，我都一定会去，哪怕这意味着第二天早上整个人彻底处于废人状态。

如果给你拍一部传记电影，宣传标语会是什么？
“一部什么都没被偷走，却人人都拿到了报酬的劫盗大片。”

aiStories.title: Vessev造出了一艘几乎是在“飞行”的电动水翼渡轮
aiStories.originalTitle: Vessev built an electric ferry that almost flies
aiStories.snippet: Vessev hopes its electric hydrofoil ferry will change the way people and cities think about boats.
aiStories.fullContent:
“When will we start flying?” I asked Vessev co-founder and CEO Eric Laakmann, as we pulled away from the Brooklyn marina in the startup’s VS-9 electric ferry. “We already are.”

I’ll admit I was a bit disappointed. I thought the moment when it transitioned from sailing like a regular boat to almost-flying as a surface-skimming hydrofoil would be more … momentous.

I’ve been on my share of boats, including large ferries, small sailboats, and plenty of others in between, but never been on a hydrofoil and I was curious what flying along the water might feel like during the brief ride from the Brooklyn Marina out toward Governors Island on the East River in New York.

It didn’t feel like flying, but it was a bit like a riding in a sports car.

Traditional boats of this size — about 30 feet — start to bounce and slap the water as they gain speed. But on a hydrofoil, that’s when the foils start to do their work.

On the surface, the VS-9 looks like plenty of other catamarans. But under the hull are two wing-like structures that lift the boat as they slice through the water. Computer-controlled underwater flaps keep the ride smooth and stable. In the VS-9, most of the lifting is done by the front foil, with about 20% handled by the rear.

The rear foil also hosts the electric motor, which Vessev makes in-house. Why not outsource it? Laakmann said that it’s important to keep costs in line — eventually, you’ll have to bring production in house, so why not do it earlier in development? The only thing Vessev doesn’t build are the batteries. “Those have been commoditized,” Laakmann said.

By lifting the hull clear of the water, hydrofoils can operate more efficiently than other boats. That’s especially important for electric boats, where every kilowatt-hour counts.

Shipbuilders have been experimenting with hydrofoils for well over a century. The design offers several advantages, including lower drag and a smoother ride. The subtle transition I experienced on the VS-9, from sailing to almost-flying, underlined just how smooth a hydrofoil can be.

Despite hydrofoils’ advantages, they’re not a panacea. The design works best in waters the boat can clear when sailing on its foils. For the VS-9, that’s about two and a half feet, or 0.75 meters. If the waves go higher than that, they start hitting the hull, ruining the smooth ride and sapping some efficiency. While they’re not ideal for the open ocean, hydrofoils make sense for other waterways, including lakes, rivers, and bays.

Vessev, which raised a $19 million Series A in August, is targeting transit operations to start. Laakmann thinks the combination of electric propulsion and hydrofoils can bring down the cost of operating smaller vessels and make them comfortable enough that they could augment urban mass transit systems.

Somewhere like New York City could use them to zip people to Brooklyn or Queens without needing to build much new infrastructure.

Hotels and tour operators are also an early target market, and public demonstrations like the one I attended have attracted wealthy individuals looking for another toy, Laakmann said.

For now, the VS-9 I rode is one of a kind, but Laakmann said Vessev plans to build more. Eventually, the company might shift to producing electric hydrofoil kits, allowing other boatbuilders to design their own vessels around the technology, Laakmann said.

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. “我们什么时候开始起飞？”当这艘初创公司的VS-9电动渡轮驶离布鲁克林码头时，我向Vessev联合创始人兼首席执行官埃里克·拉克曼（Eric Laakmann）问道。“我们已经在飞了。”

我承认当时我有点失望。我还以为从像普通船只那样航行过渡到像贴水掠过的水翼艇那样“几乎在飞行”的时刻，会显得更加……惊心动魄。

我坐过不少船，包括大型渡轮、小型帆船以及介于两者之间的各种船只，但从未坐过水翼艇；在从布鲁克林码头出发、沿纽约东河驶向总督岛的短暂行程中，我很好奇贴水飞行的感觉会是怎样的。

它感觉并不像在飞，但有点像坐在一辆跑车里。

这种尺寸（约30英尺）的传统船只在加速时会开始颠簸并拍打水面。但在水翼船上，那正是水翼开始大显身手的时刻。

表面上看，VS-9与许多其他双体船颇为相似。但在船体下方有两个翼状结构，在切开水面时将船体托起。由计算机控制的水下襟翼使航行保持平稳。在VS-9上，大部分升力由前水翼提供，后水翼承担约20%。

后水翼还搭载了由Vessev自主制造的电动机。为什么不外包？拉克曼表示，控制成本非常重要——最终你总得转为自研自产，那么为什么不在研发早期就这么做呢？Vessev唯一不自行制造的是电池。“那些已经是高度商品化的通用产品了，”拉克曼说。

通过将船体完全抬离水面，水翼船的运行效率比其他船只更高。这对于每一度电（千瓦时）都至关重要的电动船只尤为关键。

造船工人对水翼的探索已有了一个多世纪。这种设计具有多项优势，包括阻力更小、行驶更平稳。我在VS-9上体验到的那种从航行到“几乎在飞”的细微过渡，恰恰凸显了水翼船究竟有多平稳。

尽管水翼具有种种优势，但它们并非万灵药。这种设计在水波高度不影响船只依靠水翼抬起航行的水域中表现最佳。对VS-9而言，这个高度约为2.5英尺（约0.75米）。如果浪高超过这一标准，波浪就会开始冲击船体，破坏平稳的乘坐感并降低部分效率。虽然它们并不适合公海大洋，但水翼船对于湖泊、河流和海湾等其他水路非常契合。

今年8月刚完成1900万美元A轮融资的Vessev，首先将目标瞄准了公共交通运营。拉克曼认为，电力推进与水翼的结合能够降低小型船只的运营成本，并提供足够的舒适度，从而可以补充城市大众交通运输系统。

像纽约市这样的地方可以利用它们快速将乘客送往布鲁克林或皇后区，而无需新建太多基础设施。

拉克曼表示，酒店和旅游运营商也是早期的目标市场，像我参加的这种公开演示活动还吸引了寻找新玩具的富裕人士。

目前，我乘坐的VS-9还是独一无二的原型船，但拉克曼表示Vessev计划建造更多。他提到，最终该公司可能会转向生产电动水翼套件，允许其他造船厂围绕这项技术设计自己的船只。

Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

David Robinson used to write safety reports at OpenAI and now says its culture is ‘broken’

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

David Robinson used to write the safety reports that accompanied every major model release at OpenAI. This week, he resigned from his position and is now speaking out in an editorial in The Atlantic.

It’s understandable if you’re feeling a bit cynical about everyone suddenly coming out of the woodwork to warn about how dangerous the thing they helped build is. They did, after all, make this mess. But that doesn’t mean we should discount their warnings.

Robinson says that the culture in industry is fundamentally broken. That this is a deeper issue than simply slapping a few new rules or regulations on how we handle training models. Silicon Valley has operated with “extreme confidence” and “perpetual sprints,” he says, building bigger and better models with “unimpeded optimism” that ignores or underestimates potential problems.

He says the time has come for AI companies to develop a sense of humility and look outside the insular, move-fast-and-break-things world of the tech industry. Specifically, he says AI needs nuclear-level safeguards:

Given today’s risks, frontier labs need to run like nuclear power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster.

Robinson is just the latest in a growing parade of researchers and safety workers who have left their positions at prominent AI firms. Jacob Coxon seems to have kicked off the exodus by quitting Anthropic and then publicly saying AI “could kill us all by the end of the decade.” He was followed by Robert O’Callahan, Bilal Chughtai, and Josh Engels at Google DeepMind, as well as Joe Benton at Anthropic.

戴维·罗宾逊曾负责撰写 OpenAI 每次重大模型发布时附带的安全报告。本周，他从该职位辞职，目前在《大西洋月刊》（The Atlantic）发表社论发声。

如果你对那些突然冒出来警告自己亲手打造的产物有多危险的人感到有些讽刺，这是可以理解的。毕竟，这个烂摊子确实是他们造成的。但这并不意味着我们应该对他们的警告置之不理。

罗宾逊表示，该行业的文化从根本上就已经崩坏了。这是一个更深层次的问题，绝非仅仅在如何处理模型训练上生硬地加上几条新规则或监管条例就能解决。他指出，硅谷一直带着“极度的自信”并在“永不停歇的冲刺”中运转，以“毫无阻碍的盲目乐观”打造更大、更好的模型，却忽视或低估了潜在的问题。

他表示，人工智能公司学会保持谦逊，并将目光投向科技行业这种固步自封、“快速行动、打破常规”的世界之外的时机已经到来。具体而言，他表示人工智能需要核电级别的安全保障：

“鉴于当今的风险，前沿实验室需要像核电站或繁忙的机场那样运转，配备多层冗余机制并进行周密、耗时的规划，以确保偶尔且不可避免的人为失误不会成为打开灾难之门的推手。”

罗宾逊只是离开知名人工智能公司的研究人员与安全从业人员队伍中最新的一员。雅各布·考克森（Jacob Coxon）似乎拉开了这场离职潮的序幕，他从 Anthropic 辞职，随后公开表示人工智能“可能会在十年内彻底消灭我们所有人”。紧随其后的有 Google DeepMind 的罗伯特·奥卡拉汉（Robert O’Callahan）、比拉尔·丘格泰（Bilal Chughtai）和乔希·恩格斯（Josh Engels），以及 Anthropic 的乔·本顿（Joe Benton）。

aiStories.title: 盘点所有能直接常驻你短信界面的AI智能体
aiStories.originalTitle: All the AI agents that can live in your text messages
aiStories.snippet: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
aiStories.fullContent:
Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.

While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.

Below are some of the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check.

For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you.

Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026.

Fambot is an AI-powered “chief of staff” for families, designed to bring together the many moving parts of family life, including school communications, sports activities, meal planning, calendars, and other day-to-day responsibilities, and turn them into an organized plan.

The service is designed to work across both an app and text messages. Fambot is available on iOS devices, Android devices, and the web, and families can also interact with it directly over SMS. Every night, Fambot automatically sends a summary of the following day, including upcoming events, to-dos, and details such as school uniform or packing requirements. Parents can reply to those messages to ask questions, check information, or make changes to their calendar.

Fambot currently connects to Gmail and Google Calendar, with support for Outlook and Apple Calendar planned for the future.

The company launched in beta in early September 2026 and has raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding. The service is currently free during the beta period, but Fambot expects to eventually charge roughly the equivalent of a Netflix subscription.

Folk is designed to be an AI assistant you can reach through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. It can remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, track flights, handle email, and perform real-world tasks such as restaurant reservations.

One distinction is that Folk runs on its own private cloud computer. It can also run code and execute multi-step tasks rather than merely responding conversationally.

Folk launched its beta in May 2026, and it’s available for free but also offers a Pro subscription for $8.33/month if you want unlimited tasks running in the background.

Instinct first made headlines after raising $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. In September 2026, it raised $1 billion, valuing it at $10 billion.

The always-available agent can take actions on your behalf, rather than simply answer questions. Users can communicate with Instinct by text or voice and connect it to the apps and services they already use, such as email, calendar, Google Workspace, and more. The company says early users have used Instinct for tasks ranging from planning trips and buying groceries to booking tickets and cancelling subscriptions.

The company remains in private beta.

Powered by Hermes agent, Iris is designed to let users delegate tasks to an AI assistant directly through iMessage. Users can connect the apps they use and hand over a task with a simple message. The agent then works through the required steps, while retaining relevant context from previous interactions. It’s also designed to follow up with users proactively rather than waiting for another request.

Martin is a general-purpose personal assistant reachable through SMS as well as phone, WhatsApp, email, Slack, and its own iOS app.

It can help manage calendars, email, reminders, tasks, notes, and communications. It can also act on behalf of users by sending messages or making phone calls, while providing daily summaries of what needs attention.

It’s a bit on the pricier side, with subscriptions starting at $21 per month.

Miso takes the personal-assistant concept and applies it specifically to travel.

It operates through iMessage and combines AI trip planning with support from a dedicated travel team. Users can arrange flights through messaging while Miso takes into account their travel preferences, loyalty points, and other priorities. Miso also gives travelers access to trip details, flight updates, along with personalized recommendations.

Ohai is another family assistant focused on helping households manage the constant stream of information and tasks involved in everyday family life.

Users can send messages, forward emails, or make voice requests, and the assistant can transform them into schedules, reminders, and plans. It can also coordinate calendars, household chores, and meals across multiple members of a family.

It includes a free basic option, but also offers different subscriptions based on family size, starting at $9.99 per month.

Similar to the other family-focused agents, the idea behind Ollie is that families already have the information they need, but it lives across school messages, calendars, task lists, and group chats. Ollie aims to bring those pieces together and keep them in sync. It can keep track of calendars, emails, reminders, tasks, and other household details, then deliver relevant information to users through text.

Its biggest differentiator from other agents is that Ollie is one of the first mainstream, family-focused AI assistants to achieve SOC 2 compliance, a widely used security standard.

Launched in June 2026, Ollie offers a free tier, as well as paid plans starting at $25 per month for 150 messages. A $100-per-month plan includes up to 1,000 messages.

Orbits also has an AI assistant that is focused on the household.

It works through both the Orbits app and text messaging, and can bring together calendars, lists, and conversations while also carrying out tasks for you. That can include searching the web, making purchases, booking restaurants, changing appointments, and requesting quotes for household services.

Additionally, Orbits can remind family members about chores, communicate with service providers, and help coordinate responsibilities beyond the immediate household.

Orbits is backed by investors like Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Speedrun fund, N49P, and Garage Capital.

Users can interact with Pally as they would with a friend while giving it access to the apps they already rely on. The assistant can connect information spread across services such as WhatsApp, Gmail, calendars, and Google Drive, helping users keep track of plans, receipts, dates, files, and other details.

There’s a free plan available, which offers features like 15 minutes of calls per month, or there are paid plans, including $25 per month for 30 minutes of calls and $100 per month for 60 minutes.

Poke launched in March 2026 as a general-purpose assistant that you can reach through text messaging. It can handle tasks involving calendars, planning, health and fitness, smart-home controls, photos, and other everyday activities.

Poke became particularly notable in June 2026 when Apple approved Poke as the first AI agent on the Apple Messages for Business platform. A month later, parent company The Interaction Company of California was acquired by AI coding startup Cognition in a deal valued in the low nine figures.

Rene is an AI personal assistant designed to be a user’s “best contact” rather than another productivity agent. It’s text-based and can turn natural-language conversations into tasks, reminders, summaries, and other follow-up actions. Rene also maintains context across conversations, allowing it to remember details and surface things that may need attention later.

Additionally, it has a browser, can write code, shop for you, as well as create slides and images.

Rene is currently available on iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

Instead of waiting for users to open an app, Skye is an “agentic homescreen” for the iPhone that analyzes information from connected services and surfaces what it thinks is relevant through contextual cards, suggestions, and daily briefings. The assistant can generate audio briefings, prepare information ahead of meetings, surface reminders, and identify potentially useful information.

The company, Signull Labs, raised about $3.6 million in seed funding in 2025. It entered private testing and beta in April 2026, and hasn’t yet announced a public release date.

Stanley is an AI content assistant aimed at content creators rather than general personal productivity. Available through iMessage, Telegram, and the web, it acts as a kind of AI head of content, helping users come up with ideas, turn them into posts, and maintain a consistent publishing schedule.

For instance, Stanley can connect to a user’s Instagram account, using that context to suggest content based on what the user has actually been doing. Users can also send voice notes, which Stanley turns into scripts, captions, and other social assets. It includes a content calendar and can schedule posts, with the broader goal of making content creation a more continuous, automated process rather than something users have to sit down and plan from scratch.

The biggest differentiator with Tomo’s personal assistant for iMessage is that, instead of being a private assistant that only you interact with, Tomo can become part of group conversations.

Also, like other agents, it’s designed to help with goals, accountability, scheduling, and everyday organization. It also has the ability to send reminders, search the web, work with calendars and email, watch videos, and edit photos.

The basic plan starts at $19.99 per month.

Town is aimed more at professional life. It gives users a “Townie,” an AI assistant designed to learn how they work and handle recurring professional tasks. It can work with email, calendars, documents, Slack, and other platforms.

In June 2026, the company raised a $55 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and Forerunner.

Wajo’s first consumer agent, Fo, can call businesses, send emails, join group chats, make bookings and purchases, and coordinate with people to complete everyday tasks.

A key part of Wajo’s approach is giving Fo its own identity. The agent has its own email address, phone number, and payment card, allowing it to interact with businesses without requiring users to hand over their own credentials.

Notably, when Fo encounters something it cannot handle on its own, Wajo says it can bring in a human assistant to finish the task.

Fo launched publicly in September 2025 with a free tier, while heavier workloads and custom agents are available through a paid Pro offering.
